info.title: Osmia local API
info.description:
The Osmia service serves this API over its Unix socket and, when configured,
on a loopback address (listen.web) and on the tailnet (listen.tailnet). There is
no authentication: the socket, the loopback interface and tailnet membership are
the boundaries. On the web and tailnet listeners, requests must carry a Host
naming the listener, and requests other than GET and HEAD must send
Content-Type: application/json. Two routes on the tailnet listener send their
own content type instead: the git fetch request and the upload of a finished
view. The service grants no cross-site preflight for them.

Request bodies are one JSON object with known, unique fields. Every failure
returns an error object with a code and a message.

host.description: The listen.web address, such as localhost:8080, or the listen.tailnet hostname.

get.summary: Follow the event stream
get.description:
A text/event-stream of frames "event: <kind>" with a JSON data line
holding the event. The first event is resync, which asks the client to read
every view again; it also replaces events a slow subscriber missed. A comment
line keeps an idle stream open.

default.description: The request failed; the error names its code and reason.

get.summary: List member sessions, state changes, unit, final and session checks and final reviews; shared chief entries and turns are included only for single-member workgroups
get.description:
Oldest-first entries from the workstream trace and its chief-of-staff
conversation. Kinds message, response, action, status and session retain their
conversation, status and agent-turn payloads. Every claimed turn is a session,
including final-review readers. Transition identifies every recorded workflow
subject, its from/to states, actor and reason.

unit_checks has one entry per unit and run. It is running once its selection is
recorded, then shows only its recorded result: passed, failed, incomplete or
superseded, with failed check links or an error. Selection gives selected and
judged counts, the optional listed total, or a full-run reason and detail.
Absent historical selections and totals remain absent.

final_checks has one entry per started attempt of a review's check run,
joining its durable start with its recorded result. Requested reviews, preparation
and retry delays do not imply running checks. Historical results without start
evidence have no attempt or started_at; each result revision remains visible.
final_review gives each review's outcome, reader and turn, blocking finding and
uncovered criterion counts, or its failure reason. Reader turns also appear as
sessions. session_checks summarizes each exploratory session check run: its result, or while it has none (still going, or interrupted) a running entry that carries the link the run printed, with no finished_at.
Unit, final and session check entries carry one optional trace_url, the
Dagger Cloud trace link the CLI printed. It comes from the result record or,
when the result has none or does not exist yet, from the start record. Captured check output remains in the trace.

brief is the delivery brief the chief of staff recorded for a final review: its
text, before_you_ship items and screenshots. It appears once per review and
shows the latest brief when it was replaced.

A started entry keeps its original place when its result arrives. Unfinished
starts survive restart without implying success or failure. Workstream events
on /v1/events tell an open client to read this feed again.

per_workstream.description: Maximum concurrent worker turns per workstream; check slots are independent.

roles.description: Factory-wide mason, reviewer, committee, architect, checks and chief slot pools, in that order.

projects.description: Every active project, ordered by the creation time of its newest workstream (feature workstream, workgroup member, design session or exploratory session; archived ones count while their creation time can be read), newest first. Projects with equal newest times, and projects without a workstream, which come last, keep the project registry's order. Read effective.active_projects for the registry's order.

commit.description: The signed commit the landing moves the base branch to.

outcome.description: landed: the base branch is at the pushed commit and the workstream is delivered. held: the router holds the landing and nothing was pushed; it is applied once the hold clears. fell-back: the upstream refused the push, so the draft pull request was marked ready and the workstream delivered. base-moved: the base branch moved, so nothing landed; the workstream is rebased, checked and reviewed again and the service lands the new commit on its own under the same decision, with no second approval. pending: the push outcome is unknown and is settled against the fetched base branch.

reason.description: Why the workstream did not land, when it did not.

can_land.description: True when the owner may approve and land the workstream: its project's delivery is jev and the workstream is assembled. Landing is still refused when checks did not pass on the pushed commit. Absent for a project that delivers by pull request or a delivered workstream.

recommendation.description: The route land or pull-request that Jev picked below the decision threshold or without applying it, from its delivery-route decision. Empty when Jev made no pick.

description.description: Sentence describing which checks ran and why.

flaky.description: Links of checks that failed and then passed on their rerun.

selection.description: Absent for historical runs and failures before selection.

source.description: Absent for results of local check runs.

trace_url.description: Dagger Cloud trace link of the run; taken from the result record, otherwise from the run's start record.

from.description: The state the subject was in when the card was opened.

machine.description: The state machine of the subject: unit, ws, final or dep.

occurrence.description: The router occurrence the card was opened for: subject, version, trigger and cause.

subject.description: The workflow subject the move changes.

version.description: The version of that state; the move applies only while the subject is still at it.

finished_at.description: Absent while the run has no recorded result.

flaky.description: Links of checks that failed and then passed on their rerun.

state.description: running marks a run with no recorded result: it is still going or was interrupted before it recorded one.

trace_url.description: Dagger Cloud trace link of the run; taken from the result record, otherwise from the run's unfinished evidence.

decided_by.description: Who decided the transition when the transition router chose it: code (the default), jev (a departure from the default), fallback (Jev could not answer and the default was committed), owner, jev_gate (one of Jev's gate decisions) or reviewer (a reviewer's verdict authorised it).

default_to.description: The state the default would have entered.

departed.description: True when Jev departed from the default to make the transition.

judgment.description: The Jev judgment record behind the decision, when there is one.

subject.description: Recorded workflow subject, such as feature, unit-upload, unit-upload-checks, final-review or question_1.

failed.description: Links of failed checks; captured output stays in the trace.

flaky.description: Links of checks that failed and then passed on their rerun.

selection.description: Absent for historical runs that did not record a selection.

trace_url.description: Dagger Cloud trace link of the run; taken from the result record, otherwise from the run's start record.

jev.description: What Jev decided about the entry when the decision came to the owner after all: an answer below the threshold, a deferral, or a pick the service refused to apply. On a delivery entry it is Jev's delivery-route decision.

land.description: The answer that approves a delivery entry and lands the workstream. Present only on a delivery entry of a project whose delivery is jev, beside the Mark ready answer.

field.description: The setting at fault, empty when the whole revision is.

message.description: The loader's error for the stored settings.

pin.description: Names the stored revision; send it with a save.

revision.description: The number of the stored revision the settings come from.

pin.description: Names the stored revision; send it with a save.

reason.description: Why the saved values are not applied.

revision.description: The number of the stored revision the settings come from.

default.description: True when the stored settings leave the setting out and Value is its default or inherited value.

effective.description: The value in the loaded configuration.

name.description: Setting name: name, upstream, fork, clone, base_branch, landing, delivery, upstream_rebase, pull_request_poll, checks_timeout, capacity.per_workstream, capacity.git_operations, hearsay_scope, hearsay_declare_repo, flake_fixes or hearsay_entities.

pending.description: True when Value differs from Effective: the stored settings hold an edit that is not yet applied.

value.description: The stored value, or the value it would take: a string, an integer, a boolean for hearsay_declare_repo and flake_fixes, or for hearsay_entities an object of local entity ID to Hearsay entity id.

delivery.description: pull-request (the default) delivers workstreams as pull requests; jev opts the project in to landing on its base branch and is refused on a project that delivers through a fork.

flake_fixes.description: True turns flake-fix workstreams on for the project: a flaky check is recorded and the chief of staff may open a workstream to fix its cause. Those workstreams' pull requests go out under the owner's name. Default false.

hearsay_declare_repo.description: True posts the project to Hearsay with its GitHub repo declared, which makes its records visible to that repository's readers. Default false.

hearsay_entities.description: Entries to set, by local entity ID, each a Hearsay entity id.

hearsay_scope.description: A Hearsay entity id, such as work:<source>:<project>, that replaces the project's default read entity.

from.description: The state the subject was in when the card was opened.

machine.description: The state machine of the subject: unit, ws, final or dep.

occurrence.description: The router occurrence the card was opened for: subject, version, trigger and cause.

subject.description: The workflow subject the move changes.

version.description: The version of that state; the move applies only while the subject is still at it.

limit.description: Configured factory-wide slot limit from config.toml. Present only for bounded pools (mason, reviewer, committee, checks, chief). Absent when unbounded is true: that pool has no factory-wide limit, which is not a limit of 0.

note.description: Plain-words explanation of an unbounded pool: no factory-wide limit, at most one turn per workstream, no configuration setting. Absent for bounded pools.

role.description: Slot pool: mason, reviewer, committee, architect, checks or chief. The checks pool uses capacity.checks (default 2) across all projects and workstreams. The chief pool uses capacity.chief (default 3) across all projects and workstreams and holds background chief-of-staff turns only; turns the owner starts take no chief slot.

scope.description: How an unbounded pool is bounded instead: per_workstream means at most one turn runs per workstream. Absent for bounded pools.

unbounded.description: True when the pool has no factory-wide limit (architect). Such an entry has no limit field, scope is per_workstream and note explains it; there is no configuration setting to raise.

used.description: Number of slots currently in use.

waiting.description: Work waiting for a slot. Check runs identify their project, workstream and unit, final review or session. Background chief turns identify their project, workstream, agent and turn, oldest first.

projects.description: Each active project's context mode, in the same order as the projects of the configuration read: by the creation time of the project's newest workstream, newest first, with ties and projects without a workstream in registry order.

preview.description: True for a waiting service-run chief preview.

project.description: Project of a waiting check run.

review.description: Final review number for a waiting final-review check run.

session.description: True for a waiting session check run; workstream identifies the session.

telemetry_root_span_id.description: Span ID of the workstream's osmia.workstream root span, the parent of its state, turn and check spans, as 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. With telemetry_trace_id it names a span context an API client can link to.

telemetry_trace_id.description: OpenTelemetry trace ID of every span Osmia sends about the workstream, as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It depends only on the workstream ID, so it is present whether or not telemetry export is configured and is the same after a restart. It is not the durable trace record store read through /v1/trace.
